name: Pekal
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Syahwin Nikelas et al. 1986. Struktur Bahasa Pekal. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa (grammar sketch).

new_statements.quote: "Tekanan" dan "nada" terdapat pada fonem vokal yang merupakan bagian suku kata, sedangkan "panjang" terdapat pada bunyi-bunyi vokal maupun konsonan. Di dalam bahasa Kepal [sic: Pekal], ketiga ciri-ciri tadi tidak membedakan arti dan hanya merupakan ciri-ciri yang berlebihan (exagerated). Kata /meli/ 'membeli', umpamanya, tidak akan berbeda artinya seandainya mempunyai ciri-ciri sebagai berikut. a. tekanan b. nada c. panjang [...] Ciri prosodi yang dapat membedakan arti dalam BP adalah "lagu kalimat" atau 'intonasi'.
new_statements.translation: "Stress" and "pitch" occur on the vowel phonemes that form part of a syllable, whereas "length" occurs on both vowel and consonant sounds. In Pekal, these three features do not distinguish meaning and are merely redundant ('exaggerated') features. The word /meli/ 'to buy', for instance, would not differ in meaning if it had the following features: a. stress b. pitch c. length [...] The prosodic feature that can distinguish meaning in Pekal (BP) is 'sentence melody', i.e. intonation.
new_statements.citation: Nikelas, Syahwin; Asni Ayub; Marah Rusmali Zainil; Syofyan Adam. 1986. Struktur Bahasa Pekal. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan.
new_statements.locator: Bab 2 Fonologi, §2.6 Ciri Prosodi (ca. pp. 13-15; page range inferred from the scanned table of contents and a page footer '15.' in the snippets, not verified on the page)
new_statements.rule_in_words: The sketch says word stress (with pitch and length) is non-distinctive/redundant in Pekal; the example shows /meli/ unchanged in meaning with stress on either syllable; only sentence-level intonation is meaning-bearing. It gives NO rule for where stress falls (no penultimate/final statement). 'phrase-level-only' is the closest fixed reading; 'unclear' would also be defensible.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the intonation examples (abihlah may de 'Habislah nasi itu'; usak di ambik, uhan menis) are sentence-level minimal pairs, not word stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level for the non-distinctiveness claim (isolated word /meli/); sentence level for intonation. §1.3 'Anggapan Dasar' also lists 'fonem suprasegmental terdiri dari tekanan, panjang, dan jeda' as a working assumption, which the §2.6 finding effectively contradicts. Quote is stitched from overlapping Google Books snippets of a no-preview volume; the sentences are verbatim per snippet but the whole page was not seen.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes 'bahasa Pekal' (BP) of Bengkulu (Ketahun, North Bengkulu / Mukomuko area) with no dialect specified in the snippets seen; Glottolog peka1242, ISO pel. Snippet scanned writes 'bahasa Kepal' once (typo for Pekal). Google Books gives 120 pages vs Glottolog 108 (probably front matter counted).
